question: Can this machine run somewhere that is not ours?
_rung_witness_comment: SHELL.md r5 asks the record to name the gate that witnesses its rung. This surface's rung is '?', so the named gate is the one that is PENDING and is the reason it is '?'. launch-gate.mjs enforces the pairing in both directions: a rung in the five requires its witness approved with evidence; '?' requires its witness pending.
rung_unsettled_because: What this domain hosts is being decided again. The dashboard that used to answer at app.webhost.systems has been withdrawn, and no replacement has been written down. A rung names the best-evidenced shipped artifact of a surface; nothing here is shipped, and the artifact a rung would have covered is going away.
surface_rung_covers: No rung is claimed here, and the portfolio nav records none either. Measured 2026-08-17: nothing on this domain executes an agent, and the dashboard at app.webhost.systems no longer resolves. What is in the tree is listed below, and every row cites the file that settles it.
_token_comment: {{probe.KEY}} in any RENDERED string below is substituted at build time with the value that probe re-derived off disk. No count in this record is typed. launch-gate.mjs refuses a rendered field that contains a multi-digit run outside an ISO date, or a number spelled as a word, because both are how a hand-typed count gets back in — the first draft of this file said 'eleven specification documents' and the probe counted ten.

status.statement: {{probe.edge_functions}} webhost edge functions, {{probe.migrations}} database migrations and a React dashboard exist in this repository, and {{probe.tests}} tests pass across {{probe.test_files}} files. None of it reaches a runtime: the deploy path writes a database row and marks the provider reference simulated, and the invocation endpoint answers from OpenRouter. The rung is left at ? because what this domain hosts is being decided again.
status.source: Measured 2026-08-17, in this repository and against the live domain. The test count is re-run by build-site.mjs on every build, not carried in prose. Every file citation below is a path, a line number and the text on that line, recomputed at build time and refused on drift. The domain checks were curl and getent, and the commands are printed beside their results.
status.limit: This establishes that a control plane exists in a repository and that its tests pass in a Node process against mocked clients. It does not establish that anything here has ever executed an agent, that any of it has run outside a developer's machine, that the schema underneath it will survive — the shared Supabase data layer it depends on was abandoned by ruling on 2026-07-30 — or that whatever this domain hosts next will resemble what is described here. The strongest thing on this page is a list of things that are not built.

advance.requires: A decision about what this domain hosts, and a written specification for it. Until then no rung above ? is available, and inventing one is precisely what this page has just finished retracting.

artifacts.name: The control plane
artifacts.detail: A webhost.* Postgres schema with row-level security, RPCs and cron, plus {{probe.edge_functions}} edge functions: deploy, activate-deployment, invoke, delegated-invoke, telemetry and billing-webhook. Deployments are rows with a per-agent unique version, and rollback moves an active-deployment pointer rather than editing history.
artifacts.witness: The functions and migrations are counted off disk by this build and checked against the frozen record. The row it writes is the artifact; nothing is shipped to a runtime.

artifacts.name: The dashboard
artifacts.detail: Vite, React and TypeScript against a Supabase client. Agents, deployments, invocation and telemetry views, with the runtime provider chosen from a select element.
artifacts.witness: {{probe.tests}} tests pass across {{probe.test_files}} files, re-run by this build. They exercise components and library code in a jsdom process against mocked clients — no network, no database, no runtime.

artifacts.name: The v1 specification set
artifacts.detail: {{probe.spec_docs}} documents: the master spec, API contracts, the runtime provider interface, the data model, security, observability and billing, the testing plan, the [&] Protocol integration, an index and a realignment plan. Written to be implementation-ready.
artifacts.witness: Documents. Several carry a supersession banner over their data-layer half, and the runtime provider interface has no implementation on either side of it.

unmeasured.name: Execution on any runtime
unmeasured.detail: The deploy function inserts a deployment row and returns. Its own source says so on the line this page cites, and it writes a simulated marker into the provider reference. Nothing is handed to Cloudflare Workers, and there is no AWS or Bedrock dependency anywhere in the tree.
unmeasured.needs: A provider adapter that makes a real call and a real artifact to hand it. The interface is specified; neither side of it is written.

unmeasured.name: AWS Bedrock AgentCore
unmeasured.detail: It is a string. It appears as a member of a TypeScript union, as the value of an option element in the dashboard, and as a member of a Postgres enum. That is the whole of it.
unmeasured.needs: An AWS account, a dependency, and an adapter. Not one of those exists here.

unmeasured.name: The [&] Protocol integration
unmeasured.detail: Capability manifests, MCP sidecars, agent-to-agent routing and governance enforcement are written down in the integration spec and implemented nowhere. No code in this repository or in its edge functions reads an ampersand.json.
unmeasured.needs: A manifest reader, and a product decision about whether this is still the shape.

unmeasured.name: An SDK and a command line
unmeasured.detail: The workspace declares packages/* and there is no packages directory on disk. This build recomputes that on every run, so the day one appears the page can no longer say this.
unmeasured.needs: A package worth publishing, which needs a product worth wrapping.

unmeasured.name: A data layer that is not abandoned
unmeasured.detail: Everything above stands on the shared Supabase instance, and that route was abandoned by ruling on 2026-07-30 in favour of studbook. Studbook is a draft spec with no implementation, blocked on one unruled question about where confidentiality comes from. Nothing migrates until it can hold the same data with the same guarantees.
unmeasured.needs: That question answered, then an implementation. Neither is scheduled here.
unmeasured.built: no, and blocked on a ruling

zero_counts.label: Agents this platform has executed
zero_counts.witness: The deploy path stops at a database row. The invocation endpoint reaches a model provider. Neither of those is an agent running on a runtime, and this page said otherwise for months.

zero_counts.label: AWS or Bedrock packages in the tree
zero_counts.witness: Every dependency manifest in this repository is read by this build and searched for aws, bedrock and agentcore. A single match refuses the build, which is the only way a page can keep saying there are none.

zero_counts.label: Runtimes this control plane can reach
zero_counts.witness: The runtime provider interface is specified and has no implementation on either side. There is a select element whose values name providers, and no code behind any of them.

gates._comment: A gate may not read approved without its evidence, reviewer and date fields, and launch-gate.mjs enforces that.

surface_rung_settled.label: Which rung this surface may claim
surface_rung_settled.description: The named witness for this surface's rung, and it is pending on purpose. What this domain hosts is being decided again; the dashboard it fronted has been withdrawn and no replacement is written down. Until a decision exists there is no shipped artifact for a rung to name, so the chip reads ? and this gate is why.
